text: We evaluated an auxiliary confidence loss on the strong student, with an auxiliary loss weight of 0.5, in a weak-to-strong setup pairing a pythia-410m supervisor with a mistral-7b student, across 10 seeds. The weak supervisor reached an accuracy of 0.67 and the strong model's ceiling accuracy was 0.83, while the student trained on weak labels reached a transfer accuracy of 0.74 with a standard error of 0.01. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.42 with a standard error of 0.04, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.41. This difference falls well within two standard errors of the baseline, so the data do not support treating the auxiliary confidence loss as an improvement over the baseline; the observed ordering is compatible with noise at this sample size. Readers should also note that only one auxiliary loss weight and one model pair were tested, so the finding does not speak to other configurations.
